articles.title: Home Assistant builds dashboard sections across rooms and floors
articles.dek: Choose lights, batteries or other controls to include, and the section follows later additions and removals.
body: Home Assistant adds dashboard sections that fill themselves with matching controls and readings, updating as devices are added or removed. An owner can choose lights on a floor, batteries in selected rooms or other combinations, then group the tiles by room, floor or type.

A visual picker previews automatic sections and opens their editor before adding them to the dashboard. This extends the earlier device-specific sections with creation through the interface and selections spanning rooms, floors and labels, including exclusions.

pullRequests.title: Add an entities section strategy
Add a dialog to choose the type of section to create

media.alt: Home Assistant section picker showing automatic section previews

articles.title: ESPHome touchscreens control a remote browser dashboard
articles.dek: Taps and drags turn a panel showing a remote dashboard into a way to operate it.
body: ESPHome adds interaction to its remote-screen display. A connected touchscreen sends taps and drags to the computer running the dashboard, while automation actions send pointer movements, keyboard keys or text.

The VNC connection, which shares the computer’s screen, shows incoming changes immediately for two seconds after an input so taps receive a prompt visual response. This adds the controls missing from the view-only display covered on October 23; password support remains separate work.

pullRequests.title: [vnc] Add input actions and touchscreen forwarding

articles.title: Home Assistant hands Matter sharing straight to Apple Home
articles.dek: A direct handoff replaces copying a pairing code or reaching for a second device.
body: Home Assistant adds an Add to Apple Home button to the Matter device-sharing dialog in its iPhone app. The button opens Apple’s setup flow on the same phone and preserves the device’s Home Assistant name, avoiding a copied code or a QR scan with another device.

The sharing dialog also recognizes when a code is close to expiring and offers a fresh one. The iPhone handoff reads the existing Matter QR information; it does not require a second device to scan the code.

pullRequests.title: Share a Matter device to Apple Home from the frontend
Share a Matter device through the companion app from the share dialog
Document sharing a Matter device from the companion app

media.alt: Matter sharing dialog with an Add to Apple Home button

articles.title: Home Assistant makes past actions reusable from its Tools panel
articles.dek: Open an earlier action, run it again or copy its YAML for an automation.
body: Home Assistant adds an action-history page to Tools, giving owners a place to inspect earlier actions. Its detail dialog includes a Perform again button for repeating the action.
The same dialog can copy the action as YAML, including its target and data. That provides a starting point for turning a working action into a script or automation without retyping its settings.

pullRequests.title: Add action history page to tools
Add perform again button to action history detail dialog
Add copy as YAML button to action history detail dialog

media.alt: Home Assistant action-history page in the Tools panel

articles.title: Home Assistant separates a restored iPhone from the phone it copied
articles.dek: Choose a new device identity or deliberately replace the old phone’s registration.
body: A restored iPhone can carry another phone’s Home Assistant registration and sign-in, causing both phones to report as one device and letting a sign-out on one break the other. The Companion app detects that copied registration and asks whether the restored phone should become a new device or replace the old one.

Setting up a new device signs in again and creates an independent registration while leaving the original phone alone. Replacing the old device explicitly takes over its registration. Until the choice is settled, the restored phone holds back location and sensor reports that would otherwise overwrite the other phone’s readings.

pullRequests.title: Let a restored device register as a new device

articles.title: Music Assistant’s phone app lets listeners choose where to search
articles.dek: A source picker, shared recent searches and a genre filter bring the phone’s search closer to the web player.
body: Music Assistant’s phone app lets listeners choose which music services to search, alongside their own library. The choice replaces the library-only switch and is shared with the web player, so moving between the two keeps the same search sources.

Andrii Mitnovych also adds the five most recent searches and restores the genre filter. Opening or playing a result saves its search term; genre searches stay within the library because the music providers do not return genres. Source selection and genre search require Music Assistant server 2.10 or newer.

pullRequests.title: Pick the search sources, like the web frontend
Save recent searches in the server preferences
Add the Genre filter to search

articles.title: ESPHome opens Beken boards to wired sensors
articles.dek: Existing I²C sensor components gain the connection they need on BK72xx hardware.
body: ESPHome adds the two-wire I²C sensor connection to Beken BK72xx boards, letting existing sensor components work on hardware that previously lacked that support. Makers choose two pins for the connection. Testing on a BK7231N board read temperature and humidity from a CHT8305 sensor using the HDC1080 component.

A related GPIO correction ensures that Beken and Realtek pins take the intended level when switching to output. That addresses a one-wire bus stuck low and improves the new software I²C bus. The I²C implementation runs in software, so transfers briefly occupy the device’s main loop and the actual clock rate is below the configured value.

pullRequests.title: [i2c] Add software I2C bus for BK72xx
[libretiny] Apply a level written before a pin becomes an output
[i2c] Document the software I2C bus on BK72xx

articles.title: Home Assistant gives multi-part devices a clearer structure
articles.dek: MQTT outlets and supported Z-Wave components can appear beneath their parent device.
body: Home Assistant expands child-device support to MQTT and supported multi-part Z-Wave devices, so a power strip’s outlets or an energy meter’s clamps can appear as distinct parts of the physical device. MQTT publishers can describe those parts in discovery messages or YAML, while Z-Wave uses explicit labels and groups in its device database.

For example, an Aeotec ZWA046 meter becomes a main device with three clamp children, keeping its aggregate readings on the main device. Existing Z-Wave entity IDs stay the same, and automations targeting the main device still reach its children. Display names change to follow the child device.

The Z-Wave change also removes a redundant slat-cover entity on the Fibaro FGR223 and Shelly Qubino Wave Shutter; owners who explicitly enabled it lose that extra entity. A related registry change preserves a main entity’s room placement when it moves to a child device.

pullRequests.title: Add MQTT child device support
Add Z-Wave child devices
Give new child device the area of its main entity

articles.title: ZHA follows a USB adapter onto an ESPHome proxy
articles.dek: Moving the same radio between a local USB port and a network proxy updates its connection automatically.
body: Home Assistant adds automatic connection updates when a ZHA USB adapter moves from a local port to an ESPHome USB serial proxy. ZHA recognizes the adapter’s new path instead of continuing to use its old location.
The move works in either direction, including bringing the same adapter back to a local USB port.

pullRequests.title: Add ESPHome USB serial proxy roaming support to ZHA

articles.title: Linux Voice Assistant recovers from a failed microphone
articles.dek: A lost audio stream no longer leaves the assistant looking online while it cannot hear anything.
body: Linux Voice Assistant tries to reopen its microphone after a failed audio stream, such as one caused by a computer waking from sleep, a USB interruption or an audio-server restart. Previously, the recording thread stopped while the rest of the process stayed online in Home Assistant, leaving an apparently working assistant unable to hear requests.
Florian Asche adds an immediate retry and a second attempt two seconds later. If neither works, the whole process exits with an error so a configured Docker or systemd restart policy can restart it.

pullRequests.title: Reconnect the microphone after a failed stream and exit if it does not recover

articles.title: Home Assistant restores camera live view on Echo Show
articles.dek: Compatible cameras exposed through Home Assistant Cloud gain the live-view connection Alexa expects.
body: Home Assistant adds the camera interface Echo Show expects for live viewing through Home Assistant Cloud. Cameras could appear in Alexa while a request such as “show the porch camera” did nothing, because the older streaming interface no longer supplied the live-view path.

The change applies to cameras with native WebRTC support or a provider such as go2rtc. The contributor tested a real Echo Show with UniFi Protect cameras through Home Assistant Cloud, confirming both spoken requests and the Alexa app’s Live View button.

pullRequests.title: Add Alexa.RTCSessionController support for camera live view on Echo Show
Document Alexa WebRTC live view for Echo Show cameras

articles.title: ESPHome saves startup errors for the next log connection
articles.dek: An optional buffer preserves messages written before Wi-Fi is ready.
body: ESPHome adds an optional startup log buffer so a device can explain an early failure after a log client connects. It preserves messages that appeared before Wi-Fi was ready, including when a shared or unavailable serial port leaves no other way to read them.

Makers choose the buffer size and can retain extra detail for a particular component. A replay action sends the stored lines to log listeners with their original time since startup. Capture stops at the first replay, and a warning reports any lines that did not fit.

pullRequests.title: [logger] Add optional boot log buffer replayed over the API
[logger] Document the boot log buffer and replay action

articles.title: Music Assistant tunes ABC radio to the listener’s state
articles.dek: Regional streams and song details replace a New South Wales-only selection.
body: Music Assistant’s ABC Radio provider lets listeners select their Australian state for regional streams and the matching song information. Previously, its station selection and now-playing lookup were tied to New South Wales, which could put listeners elsewhere on the wrong feed when local schedules or daylight-saving arrangements differed.
The regional choice covers Triple J, Double J, ABC Classic and ABC Kids. The change is genesispc’s first contribution to Music Assistant’s server.

pullRequests.title: Update ABC Radio Network Provider to support multiple states in Australia

articles.title: Z-Wave JS UI recovers from old HTTPS certificates
articles.dek: Automatic certificate replacement prevents an upgrade from trapping older installations in a restart loop.
body: Z-Wave JS UI repairs startup for installations whose automatically generated HTTPS certificate is too old for the newer runtime. A stored 1024-bit key could cause repeated crashes after upgrading to 11.25.0. Rejected built-in certificates are now backed up and replaced with a new 2048-bit pair.

Custom certificates follow a stricter path: invalid or missing files stop startup with an explanation instead of silently substituting a self-signed certificate. Installations relying on that fallback must fix their custom certificate settings or remove both custom file settings.

pullRequests.title: fix(https): regenerate self-signed certs rejected by Node 24

articles.title: ZHA respects a thermostat’s actual fan speeds
articles.dek: Compatible thermostats can expose low, medium and high settings instead of only Auto and On.
body: The ZHA library reads the fan modes advertised by a thermostat instead of assuming every fan offers only Auto and On. Compatible devices can expose low, medium and high speeds and report the selected setting correctly.
A separate fan-only operating mode requires an explicit device-specific opt-in. Having a fan-control interface alone does not establish that the thermostat supports fan-only operation.

pullRequests.title: Fix thermostat fan modes to respect `fan_mode_sequence`

articles.title: Music Assistant gives way when another app takes over Sonos
articles.dek: Switching to television or another app releases the old music session instead of leaving Music Assistant in control.
body: Music Assistant gives up its Sonos queue when another app or audio source takes over a speaker, including when a Sonos Arc switches to television sound. It stops sending commands for the old session rather than continuing to treat that session as its own.

When someone starts music again, Music Assistant loads it into the session already playing instead of creating a new session that first stops the speaker. Michael N supplies the changes to the Sonos connection.

pullRequests.title: Handle Sonos coordinator moves, session takeovers and announcement clip status

articles.title: Home Assistant shortens the wait for large energy histories
articles.dek: Batched statistics work cuts the time spent importing readings and changing their units.
body: Home Assistant reduces the work needed to show and maintain long statistics histories. The Energy year view builds its monthly results as readings arrive from the database, while imports and unit conversions update records in batches instead of handling each row separately.

In the contributor’s generated test database, the Energy year query fell from 350 to 180 milliseconds. Changing the unit of a ten-year history on SQLite fell from seventeen seconds to 1.1 seconds, reducing the time that operation occupies the recorder. These are local measurements; the resulting statistics matched the earlier output.

pullRequests.title: Stream statistics rows and reduce per statistic
Use bulk queries when importing statistics
Use bulk update when changing statistics unit

articles.title: Music Assistant’s desktop volume leaves calls alone
articles.dek: New companion-player setups control music volume without changing the computer’s system level.
body: Music Assistant’s desktop companion player defaults to software volume control, so adjusting music volume does not change the level of calls or other applications. David Bishop’s change applies to new installations and settings without a saved volume mode. Existing saved choices stay as they are.

pullRequests.title: Default to software volume control

articles.title: Home Assistant gives screen readers clearer dashboard controls
articles.dek: Tiles stop speaking twice, and buttons name the action and room they affect.
body: Home Assistant makes dashboard tiles easier to use with a screen reader. A tile acting as a button is announced once, and its icon describes the action—such as toggling a floor lamp—instead of repeating the tile’s name.

Brightness and other controls are grouped under their card’s name, and area-wide light buttons say which room they affect. Climate and humidifier status badges also gain spoken alternatives, such as Heating.

pullRequests.title: Improve a11y for tile cards and area light buttons
